evidence: `cargo test -p tank_core --test habitat_registry` passed: 24/24 habitat-registry unit tests are green.
`cargo test -p tank_core --test save_load legacy_schema_v4_saves_preserve_trim_plants_as_leave_cuttings -- --exact` passed, so legacy-save loading still materializes a non-empty registry.

Runtime probe against `tank_scenarios::seeded_state(SimSeed(42), "medium_planted")` showed the stored registry is stale on startup: `GlassHardscape` live/recomputed area `2860/5760` cm², `PlantSurfaces` `275/325` cm², `SubstrateSurface` `1000/1800` cm², `SubstrateDeep` `100/3060` cm².

Runtime probe after `TrimPlantsAndRemove { fraction: 0.5 }` followed by `step_hours(1)` showed `PlantSurfaces` stayed at `275` cm² in `state.habitat_registry` while `compute_habitat_registry(state)` returned `137.5` cm²; total plant biomass had already dropped to `4.0` g at day `0`, hour `1`.

Code inspection confirms the sync gap: `crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:56-105` computes the registry once in `TankState::new`; `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:531-549` and `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:552-656` overwrite geometry/substrate/plants/hardware without rebuilding it; `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:352-355` is the only automatic recompute site, while actions in `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:600-715` mutate habitat inputs without any registry refresh.
findings_or_gaps: High: `TankState.habitat_registry` is not maintained as a canonical serialized engine concept. Scenario materialization, startup overrides, and non-daily mutations leave the stored registry inconsistent with the actual geometry/hardware/plant state until the next daily update. That directly fails the bead requirement that plant-driven areas update when biomass changes and makes saves/snapshots incorrect whenever they occur before the next daily recompute.

Medium: Coverage only exercises the pure `compute_habitat_registry()` helper. There is no regression test asserting that the stored `state.habitat_registry` matches a fresh recomputation after scenario startup, overrides, or action-driven state changes, which is how the stale-state bug escaped.
follow_up_or_amendments: Add a single refresh path for derived habitat data and call it anywhere habitat inputs can change before the next day boundary: scenario materialization, startup overrides, `Engine::from_parts`, and action/system paths that mutate plant biomass, substrate, filter, light, aeration, or other habitat inputs.

Add regression tests that compare `state.habitat_registry` with `compute_habitat_registry(&state)` after `tank_scenarios::seeded_state(...)`, after `seeded_state_with_full_overrides(...)`, and after at least one post-action hourly step such as plant trimming.

Decide explicitly whether `habitat_registry` is authoritative persisted state or a derived cache. If it is derived, recompute it on load/save boundaries as well; if it is authoritative, every mutating path must update it immediately.
